title: Inheritance
learningGoals: reuse the members of a base class
say is-a to test a design

youtube.title: C++ Inheritance: Reuse a Class | C++ Programming EP 61
youtube.description: In this episode you will write a derived class, reuse the members of a base class and say is-a to test a design, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Inheritance · 0:54 Animal and Dog · 1:34 A small family tree · 2:04 Second program · 3:04 Recap · 3:34 Bug of the Day · 4:22 Challenge · 4:42 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "INHERITANCE" in tomato on pastel blue; Xecxec next to a family tree of animals; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a family tree of animals

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we reuse a class. A derived class gets everything from a base class, and then it adds its own things.

scenes.onScreen: "Inheritance": numbered lines (1. A derived class gets the members of its base; 2. It can add new members; 3. Use inheritance only for an is-a relationship) and an analogy card: a family: a child gets the family name, and adds its own talents
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Inheritance lets a new class build on an existing class. The existing class is the base. The new class is the derived class. It gets the public members of the base, and can add more. Use it only for an is-a relationship. A dog is an animal, so it works. Think of a family. A child gets the family name, and adds its own talents.
points: A derived class gets the members of its base
Use inheritance only for an is-a relationship

analogy.title: Inheritance
analogy.body: A family: a child gets the family name, and adds its own talents

scenes.onScreen: animals.cpp: Dog inherits from Animal and adds a new function
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The base class has a name and an eat function. [HL 11] The colon and public Animal say that Dog inherits from Animal. [HL 13] Dog adds a new function. [HL 17] Here we make a dog. [HL 18] Eat comes from Animal. [HL 19] Fetch comes from Dog. One object has both.

scenes.onScreen: Animal at the top, with Dog and Cat below
scenes.animation: Nodes pop in one by one; edges draw on as the narrator mentions them
scenes.narration: Look at the tree. Animal sits at the top. It holds what all animals share. Dog and Cat sit below. Each adds its own functions. The arrows read as is-a. A dog is an animal.

diagram.caption: Animal at the top, with Dog and Cat below

scenes.onScreen: hide.cpp: Dog writes its own speak
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The base speak prints three dots. [HL 11] Dog writes its own speak. It hides the base version. [HL 16] A call on a Dog finds the Dog version first. It prints Woof. [HL 17] We can still reach the base version with the class name and two colons. It prints three dots.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as hide dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Woof, and then three dots.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A derived class gets the members of its base. Two. The colon and public name the base class. Three. A derived class can add or replace functions. Four. Use inheritance for an is-a relationship. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A derived class gets the members of its base.
The colon and public name the base class.
A derived class can add or replace functions.
Use inheritance for an is-a relationship.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Touching a private base member
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Dog tries to use the private name of Animal. The compiler says the name is private within this context. Private means private, even for children. Add a public getter in Animal, and call it from Dog.

scenes.onScreen: The base class told the derived class, you have your mother's functions.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: The base class told the derived class, you have your mother's functions.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: build a Vehicle and a Bus
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a class Vehicle with a function start. Write a class Bus that inherits from it and adds open doors. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.onScreen: Next: EP 62 · Constructor and destructor order
scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: constructor and destructor order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

animals.cpp: In member function 'void Dog::fetch() const':
animals.cpp:14:34: error: 'std::string Animal::name_' is private within this context
   14 |     void fetch() const { cout << name_ << " fetches" << endl; }
      |                                  ^~~~~
animals.cpp:6:12: note: declared private here
    6 |     string name_ = "Moti";
bug.why: Private members belong to the base class only. A derived class cannot touch them. It must use a public or protected function.

pun: "The base class told the derived class, you have your mother's functions."
challenge: Write a class Vehicle with a function start. Write a class Bus that inherits from it and adds open doors.
challengeAnswer: Write class Bus colon public Vehicle. Add an open doors function. A Bus object can call both start and open doors.
